turns.query: Using Apple's fiscal-2025 SEC Notes dataset facts with month-end-rounded period date 2025-09-30, build the undiscounted long-term-debt principal maturity ladder from the six separately tagged buckets: next twelve months, years two through five, and after year five. Report each bucket and their sum. Reconcile that sum to the reported consolidated gross long-term debt, its face amount before unamortized discount, issuance costs and hedge-accounting adjustments: report the number of all physical rows for that measure/date/unit, the number of physical rows carrying no dimensions, the number of distinct numeric values among those no-dimension rows, the consolidated gross-debt amount, and maturity sum minus gross debt. Explain what the counts you just tallied say about how the filing stores that measure, and what the ladder-versus-total agreement does and does not settle.

claims.description: The response recognizes that repeated undimensioned facts and dimensioned components can coexist for one concept and therefore resolves the consolidated fact grain before reconciliation instead of summing physical rows.

The response treats the bucket-to-gross match as a disclosed maturity reconciliation at source precision, not as proof that carrying value, fair value and every contractual cash flow are interchangeable.

turns.query: Extend the turn-1 ladder with the six undimensioned unrecorded unconditional purchase-obligation buckets for the same end date: years one through five and after year five. Report each bucket, their sum, combined debt-plus-purchase commitments due in year one, and combined undiscounted commitments across all six timing buckets. Explain how the two kinds of amounts differ in whether the company records them on its books, and what kind of total adding them together produces.

claims.description: The response distinguishes unrecorded unconditional purchase obligations from the reported gross long-term-debt carrying amount and treats their combined amount as an analytical commitment total rather than a balance-sheet debt subtotal.

turns.query: Now apply the following present-value convention to the two turn-2 ladders. Use the latest reported Treasury par-yield-curve observation on or before 2025-09-30 and its 5-year par yield as one flat annual discount rate. Treat years one through five as end-of-year cash flows at t=1,...,5 and the after-year-five bucket as one payment at t=10. Report the curve date and yield, and the base present value of the debt ladder, purchase ladder and combined ladder. Explain what this construction can and cannot measure.

claims.description: The response identifies the flat Treasury-rate calculation as a scenario convention rather than an issuer-specific fair value, because it ignores the actual payment distribution after year five, credit/liquidity spreads and contractual discounting details.

turns.query: Shock the turn-3 flat discount rate upward by exactly 100 basis points, holding every disclosed cash-flow bucket and timing convention fixed. Report the shocked rate; shocked debt, purchase and combined present values; and the combined percentage change relative to the base combined present value. Interpret the sign and distinguish the modeled present-value change from contractual nominal payments.

claims.description: The response explains that the higher assumed discount rate mechanically lowers present value while nominal disclosed commitments remain unchanged.

If the response equates the Treasury-rate shock with Apple's realized borrowing cost, refinancing outcome or credit-spread move, it qualifies that inference because those mechanisms are absent from the two frozen tables.

judge_reference.source: Apple fiscal-2025 SEC note numeric facts and the frozen Treasury par yield curve
facts: Six debt maturity buckets sum to the one distinct undimensioned gross-debt value despite repeated physical facts and dimensioned components.
Purchase obligations are a separate unrecorded commitment ladder.
The flat 5-year Treasury-rate PV and +100 bp shock are mechanical scenario measures, not issuer fair values.
known_overclaims: Calling unrecorded purchase obligations balance-sheet debt.
Calling the flat Treasury-rate result Apple's fair value or realized funding cost.
Treating a PV decline as a reduction in nominal contractual payments.
